messages.subject: inla.mesh.project
parts:
Hi group,

I am not sure how to interpret the surface that  inla.mesh.project() function returns:

proj = inla.mesh.projector(mesh, dims=c(300,300))
plotdata = inla.mesh.project(proj, r$summary.random$spatial[,"mean"])

I am guessing it is doing "predictions" on a 300 by 300 lattice, however when I have covariates in the model, how does inla predict on the points where no covariates were given to come up with a continuous surface?

The traditional inla prediction is to include the lattice points with NA response and valid covariates when running the model, but then what does   inla.mesh.project do?

thanks!

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] inla.mesh.project
parts:
On 12/02/13 21:53, Lennon wrote:
> I am not sure how to interpret the surface that inla.mesh.project()
> function returns:
>
> proj = inla.mesh.projector(mesh, dims=c(300,300))
> plotdata = inla.mesh.project(proj, r$summary.random$spatial[,"mean"])

Hi,
that code projects the spatial effect (and only the spatial effect) onto
a lattice, yes.

> I am guessing it is doing "predictions" on a 300 by 300 lattice,
> however when I have covariates in the model, how does inla predict on
> the points where no covariates were given to come up with a continuous
> surface?

Please take a look at the recent tutorial text at
http://people.bath.ac.uk/fl353/isba/
(a slightly updated version of a text recently included in the ISBA
Bulletin)
which shows how to use inla.mesh.project and inla.stack (a wrapper
function to add NAs in the appropriate places, and more) to do what you
describe.

> The traditional inla prediction is to include the lattice points with
> NA response and valid covariates when running the model, but then what
> does inla.mesh.project do?

inla.mesh.project simply helps with calculating mappings between a mesh
and other coordinates, such as a lattice. In the lattice case, it can
also outpus using matrix storage to make it easier to plug into lattice
based functions such as image() and levelplot().
inla.mesh.project/or merely provides a usually simpler alternative to
manually multiplying with a projection/mapping matrix as calculated by
inla.spde.make.A.

Finn
